sections.h2: Who to call about property tax
sections.html:
Bills come from the Trustee, and value questions go to the Assessor of Property. The Trustee works from the courthouse in Athens, and the County Commission sets the rate.

  • Trustee: McMinn County Courthouse, 6 East Madison Avenue, Athens, TN 37303. Phone (423) 745-1291, fax (423) 744-1603.
  • Hours: weekdays 8:00 to 4:00, plus Saturday mornings in February, 8:30 to noon.
  • Assessor of Property: appraises and classifies each parcel, verifies sales and handles reappraisal questions.

The Trustee's page describes three jobs for the office: collecting county property tax, keeping the county's accounts, and investing idle funds. It also runs the state tax relief program. Notices are mailed in October to whoever owned the property on January 1, and the owner must keep the mailing address current with the Assessor.

Athens is both the county seat and the biggest city. The county also holds Etowah, Niota and Sweetwater, the towns of Calhoun and Englewood, and Riceville. It had 57,404 residents on July 1, 2025, up 7.8% from April 2020, and has 24,424 housing units, 75.8% of them owner-occupied. A typical owner-occupied house is valued at $211,800, rent in the middle is $803, and household income in the middle is $61,470. Builders took out 125 permits in 2025.

School lines matter to buyers. McMinn County Schools runs most of the public schools, including McMinn County High and McMinn Central High. Athens City Schools and the Etowah School District cover grades K to 8 in their own areas, with the county high schools taking those students after eighth grade. Tennessee Wesleyan University is in Athens.

The combined county rate is $1.0823 per $100 of assessed value for the fiscal year that began July 1, 2026. The County Commission set it by Resolution 26-036 at its June 15, 2026 meeting, and the Trustee may round tax statements to the nearest whole dollar. Assessments follow state classes: 25 percent for farm and residential property, 30 percent for personal property, 40 percent for industrial and commercial property and 55 percent for public utilities.

The levy splits across six funds, and three of them are school funds for McMinn, Athens and Etowah.

McMinn County levy by fund, per $100 of assessed value

General Fund$0.4828

McMinn School Fund$0.0944

A city may add its own tax on top of the county figure, so confirm with the city whether your house owes one.

Payment opens October 1 and stays open through the last day of February without penalty. On March 1 the Trustee adds 1.5 percent per month in penalty and interest to unpaid tax.

Mail is accepted, the postmark sets the payment date, and a receipt comes back by mail. Delinquent tax is a lien that follows the parcel to any owner, so buyers are urged to run a title check for liens. The county also requires delinquent taxes to be paid before current ones, so a prior-year balance absorbs a payment aimed at this year's bill.

The office also opens on Saturday mornings in February. For payment methods beyond mail and in-person, call (423) 745-1291.

Start with the Assessor of Property, then file with McMinn County's local equalization board. State law sends a disputed value to the county board first, and a case that skips it generally becomes final. The Comptroller's appeals guide explains that the county board is a panel of five or more people who hear complaints and can change disputed assessments.

  • County board: file by the date the Assessor gives you for this year's session.
  • State Board of Equalization: August 1, or the 45th day after the county board mailed its notice if that is later.
  • Hearing: before an administrative judge, with a written decision within 90 days after the hearing.
  • Chancery court: a petition within 60 days after the state board's order is final.

Business owners should note one more rule. A forced assessment, which happens when a business fails to file a personal property schedule, can be set aside only by an appeal to the local board before that year's deadline. The schedule is due before March 1.

The Trustee runs a state-funded program for elderly and disabled homeowners and for disabled-veteran owners. When an applicant qualifies, the State of Tennessee pays a portion of the tax on the home. An application must be filed no later than 35 days after the February 28 payment deadline, which lands in early April. Programs also exist for a veteran with a 100 percent rating.

Income limits and credit amounts are set by the state each year, so call (423) 745-1291 for this year's figures before you apply. Relief repays part of a bill you have paid, so the bill itself still arrives.

sections.h2: Selling a McMinn County house with tax owed
sections.html:
Old tax stays with the house, so a buyer's title search will find any unpaid year. Delinquent tax binds the property whoever owns it, and a seller with a late balance should expect the title company to require payoff at closing.

Ask the Trustee for the amount for each tax year, interest included, before you accept an offer. If the house is inherited, behind on payments or in need of repairs, the tax balance is one more number the title company will collect from the proceeds, and knowing it early keeps the closing date from slipping.

Steps for a seller: call (423) 745-1291 for each year's balance, ask the Assessor to fix the owner name or mailing address if it is wrong, give the figures to the title company, and expect the payoff to appear on the settlement statement. A cash sale on a short timeline follows the same steps and simply moves faster.

faqs.q: What is the current McMinn County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The combined county rate is $1.0823 for every $100 of assessed value, for the fiscal year that started July 1, 2026. The County Commission set it on June 15, 2026. Residential property is assessed at 25 percent of appraised value.

faqs.q: When does McMinn County charge interest on late taxes?
faqs.a: On and after March 1. The Trustee adds 1.5 percent per month to delinquent tax, and payment is open from October 1 through the last day of February without penalty.

faqs.q: Can I mail my McMinn County property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Mailed payments are accepted and the postmark date decides whether you paid on time. The Trustee returns a receipt by mail.

faqs.q: Which school systems affect a McMinn County tax bill?
faqs.a: Three funds on the levy support schools: McMinn, Athens and Etowah. Athens City Schools and the Etowah School District serve grades K to 8 in their areas, while McMinn County Schools covers most of the rest.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay old McMinn County taxes before this year's?
faqs.a: Yes. Delinquent taxes must be paid before current taxes can be paid. A delinquent balance also attaches to the parcel whoever owns it.
